report.incidentSummary: Starting at approximately 10:05 IST (04:35 UTC) on 2026-10-09, users asking the AI assistant about their portfolios received messages stating they hold no funds, even though the Portfolio screen accurately showed their holdings. An assistant query surge starting at 10:00 IST saturated user-context-service worker threads, causing holdings context build requests to time out between 04:35 and 05:15 UTC. Upon timing out, user-context-service executed a fallback mechanism that wrote an empty context ('holdings=0 sips=0') into the shared cache with an excessive 6-hour TTL (21600 seconds). Even after the traffic surge and worker timeouts subsided at 05:15 UTC, user-context-service persistently served these poisoned zero-holdings cache records to the assistant through noon.
report.rootCauseStatement: A traffic surge on assistant-orchestrator saturated the worker pool of user-context-service, triggering context assembly timeouts. On timeout, user-context-service cached fallback empty contexts ('holdings=0 sips=0') with an excessive 6-hour TTL (21600s), causing the assistant to continuously serve cached zero-holdings responses to affected users long after worker pool saturation subsided.

hypotheses.cause: user-context-service worker pool saturated during a traffic surge, causing context build timeouts that triggered fallback writes of empty portfolio contexts ('holdings=0 sips=0') to cache with an excessive 6-hour TTL (21600s), persistently serving false zero holdings to the assistant.
hypotheses.rationale: Direct logs and metrics show that during the 04:35-05:15 UTC traffic surge (where requests peaked at 74.12 req/s and timeouts reached ~49/min), user-context-service logged worker pool saturation and executed fallback cache SETs with 'holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s'. From 05:15 UTC through 07:30 UTC, 390 requests were served directly from cache while missing_context_rate stayed elevated at ~9%, matching the persistent symptoms at noon.

hypotheses.cause: A scheduled marketing push notification campaign ('ask-sip-oct') blasted 2.1M users at 10:00 IST, directly causing the traffic surge that overwhelmed user-context-service.
hypotheses.rationale: Although assistant traffic surged at 04:30 UTC, notification-service processed only routine transactional notifications, request rate remained flat at ~330 req/s, and zero logs matching 'ask-sip-oct' or 'campaign' were found across notification-service, job-scheduler, assistant-orchestrator, or user-context-service.

hypotheses.cause: portfolio-service deployment CHG-48227 (holdings endpoint pagination fix) at 04:28 UTC degraded the holdings API or increased latency, causing upstream timeouts in user-context-service.
hypotheses.rationale: portfolio-service p95 latency remained steady at ~143 ms, p50 latency remained completely flat at ~35.5 ms, error rate held at baseline ~0.2%, and throughput remained stable across the entire window, confirming the service was completely healthy.

facts.statement: At 2026-10-09T04:28:00.000Z, portfolio-service deployed version 7.2.1 (CHG-48227) for a holdings endpoint pagination fix, which was the only deployment among scoped services.
assistant-orchestrator incoming request rate surged from 26.7 req/s at 04:25 UTC to a peak of 64.45 req/s at 04:35 UTC, remaining elevated until approximately 05:10 UTC.
user-context-service request rate surged concurrently from ~32 req/s baseline to a peak of 74.12 req/s at 04:50 UTC.
user-context-service timeout count spiked from baseline ~0.2/min to a peak of 48.84/min at 04:40 UTC, and error rate rose from ~0.3% to ~12.3% between 04:35 and 05:15 UTC.
user-context-service logged 254 events stating 'context build timed out after #ms (holdings fetch pending); worker pool #/# busy, # queued' between 04:35:01Z and 05:14:50Z.
Upon timeout, user-context-service logged WARN entries setting empty contexts into cache: 'cache SET user_ctx:u_<id> holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)'.
user-context-service missing_context_rate spiked to 23.24% at 05:00 UTC and remained elevated at 8.3% to 9.8% through 07:30 UTC.
Between 05:15:05Z and 07:29:43Z, user-context-service logged 390 events of serving context directly from cache, with user_context cache hit rate elevated at 97% to 98%.
portfolio-service p95 latency (137-153 ms), p50 latency (34-37 ms), request rate (847-1168 req/s), and error rate (0.17-0.23%) remained completely stable throughout 04:00 to 07:30 UTC.
notification-service processed only routine transactional messages (53 messages between 04:25Z and 05:30Z) with zero occurrences of 'ask-sip-oct' or 'campaign' across logs.

inferences.statement: The morning traffic surge at 10:00 IST (04:30 UTC) exhausted the internal worker pool of user-context-service, causing pending holdings build tasks to exceed their timeout threshold.

Caching the fallback zero-holdings context with an excessive 6-hour (21600s) TTL poisoned the cache for all users who queried during the surge, causing the assistant to repeatedly inform them that they held no funds through noon even after timeouts subsided.
The Portfolio screen showed holdings correctly because mobile clients query portfolio-service via api-gateway, which remained healthy and unaffected by the user-context-service worker saturation.

## Summary

An assistant query surge starting at 10:00 IST saturated user-context-service worker threads, causing holdings context build requests to time out between 04:35 and 05:15 UTC. Upon timing out, user-context-service executed a fallback mechanism that wrote an empty context ('holdings=0 sips=0') into the shared cache with an excessive 6-hour TTL (21600 seconds). Even after the traffic surge and worker timeouts subsided at 05:15 UTC, user-context-service persistently served these poisoned zero-holdings cache records to the assistant through noon.

**Root cause:** A traffic surge on assistant-orchestrator saturated the worker pool of user-context-service, triggering context assembly timeouts.
